title: Inside Trump’s Deal With the I.R.S. to Drop His $10 Billion Lawsuit
partialText: Discussions among a group of lawyers with allegiance to the president were closely held. Some senior White House officials were said to have felt blindsided as the agreement took shape.

title: Trump Administration Sees Striking Exodus of Legal Talent
partialText: The departure of more than 10,000 federal lawyers has left some agencies without sufficient staff and has boosted the ranks of state attorneys general offices and advocacy groups.

title: Pulling Customs From ‘Sanctuary’ City Airports Would Cause Chaos, Business Groups Say
partialText: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin’s proposal could block hubs like Boston, New York and Los Angeles from accepting international flights.

title: Trump Sends Tougher Peace Proposals Back to Iran, Officials Say
partialText: His changes to the proposed deal were potentially designed to speed up the process by putting pressure on Iran to accept the current framework, one official said.

title: Israel Captures Crusader Castle That Symbolized Its Long Lebanon Occupation
partialText: The seizure of Beaufort in southern Lebanon called up bitter memories in both countries amid a widening Israeli conflict with Hezbollah that seems far from over.

title: After Voting Decision, a Month of Political Earthquakes Across the South
partialText: As Republicans rush to redraw the region’s congressional maps, some voters are confused and concerned, and civil rights activists are gearing up for the fight of a generation.

title: He Was Satirized on British TV. Now He’s Trump’s Pick to Lead California.
partialText: Steve Hilton grabbed headlines when he worked in conservative politics in Britain. His American political renaissance in the California governor’s race has bemused former British colleagues and rivals.

title: Platner’s Wife Flagged His Sexual Texts With Other Women as Maine Senate Race Began
partialText: The wife of Graham Platner, the Democratic candidate in Maine, told the campaign he had sent sexual messages to other women.

title: Senator Dan Sullivan Has a New Challenger in Alaska: Dan Sullivan
partialText: Two candidates with the same name will be on the ballot seeking the same seat in the state’s primary. “It’s going to be confusing,” one Republican said.

title: In U.F.O. Files, Some Christians See Vexing Questions — and Demons
partialText: The prospect of intelligent life elsewhere in the universe raises unsettling theological implications.

title: Tilly Norwood, A.I. Actress, Wants to Know Why Everyone’s Mad at Her
partialText: The A.I. actress on her craft, the future of film and how she definitely does not intend to murder us.

title: The Museum of Wretched Ideas Has Reopened
partialText: We seem to have forgotten more or less everything.

title: How to Make Americans Read Again
partialText: The reading crisis is real, but the solution does not require new inventions.

title: Scene Stealer

title: Israel Day Parade to Return to New York Against a Changed Backdrop
partialText: Mayor Zohran Mamdani did not attend the annual Israel Day Parade, which is taking place amid a deterioration of public support for the country and rising antisemitism across the United States.

title: N.J. Governor Calls for Calm After Protesters Clash With Police at Delaney Hall
partialText: Mayor Ras Baraka of Newark imposed a curfew early Sunday around the immigration detention center after a second consecutive night of unrest over living conditions there.

title: China’s Rise in Drug Development Looms Over U.S.
partialText: Clinical trials in China are getting attention at an international oncology gathering in Chicago. China’s surging biotechnology industry is fueling alarm that U.S. dominance in the field is waning.

title: Who’s the Vegas Retiree With the Big Offer for Greenland?
partialText: Clifford E. Stanley, a retired broker, explains his unusual mission, which caught a lot of people by surprise.
